# truenas_zvol (Resource)

Manages a ZFS volume (zvol/block device) on TrueNAS. While the zvol has snapshots, destroying it fails and lists them, unless force_destroy = true.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "truenas_zvol" "iso" {
  name    = "tank/iso"
  volsize = 10737418240 # 10 GiB
}

# Renaming: changing `name` renames the zvol in place (its snapshots move with
# it, `guid` is unchanged). TrueNAS performs NO safety checks: an iSCSI extent,
# NVMe-oF namespace or VM disk that uses the old device path keeps it and the
# LUN goes offline until re-pointed. The provider refuses the rename while
# anything references the zvol unless allow_rename_in_use = true.
resource "truenas_zvol" "vm1" {
  name    = "tank/vms/vm1" # was "tank/vm1": applied as a rename
  volsize = 21474836480
  sparse  = true
}

# Cloning from a golden image: keep the golden as a zvol with a snapshot and
# boot each VM from a clone of it. The clone shares the snapshot's blocks until
# it diverges and may be larger than the golden. `origin` is create-only (a
# different origin is a different disk, so changing it replaces the zvol; the
# destroy half needs force_destroy = true). ZFS refuses to destroy a snapshot
# while clones exist: referencing the snapshot resource in `origin` makes
# Terraform destroy the clones first.
resource "truenas_zvol" "golden" {
  name    = "tank/golden/debian13"
  volsize = 10737418240
}

resource "truenas_snapshot" "golden" {
  dataset = truenas_zvol.golden.name
  name    = "v1"
}

resource "truenas_zvol" "vm2" {
  name    = "tank/vms/vm2"
  origin  = truenas_snapshot.golden.id # "tank/golden/debian13@v1"
  volsize = 21474836480               # grown beyond the golden
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Full zvol path, e.g. tank/myvol. Changing it renames the zvol in place (pool.dataset.rename): data, child datasets and snapshots move with it and the ZFS guid is unchanged. WARNING: TrueNAS performs no safety checks on a rename. SMB/NFS shares, iSCSI extents, NVMe-oF namespaces, snapshot, replication, rsync and cloud sync tasks and VM disks that point at the old path are NOT updated and break until re-pointed; a zvol under a live iSCSI extent or NVMe-oF namespace goes offline for its initiators. The provider refuses the rename while any of those reference the zvol unless allow_rename_in_use = true. Other Terraform resources that reference the zvol's name or mountpoint plan their own update (or replacement) in the same apply, so there is a window with a broken path. The pool component cannot change.
- `volsize` (Number) Volume size in bytes.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `allow_rename_in_use` (Boolean) When true, a rename proceeds even though SMB/NFS shares, iSCSI extents, NVMe-oF namespaces, snapshot/replication/rsync/cloud sync tasks or VM disks still reference the zvol or its descendants. Default false: such a rename fails and lists them. TrueNAS does not re-point any of them; Terraform-managed references plan their own update on the next apply, anything else must be fixed by hand.
- `checksum` (String) Checksum algorithm: ON, OFF, FLETCHER2, FLETCHER4, SHA256, SHA512, SKEIN, EDONR, or BLAKE3. Null inherits.
- `comments` (String) Human-readable description.
- `compression` (String) Compression algorithm. Case-insensitive: lz4, zstd, off, inherit, etc.
- `copies` (Number) Number of copies of each block (1-3). Null (unset) inherits from the parent.
- `dedup` (String) Deduplication: ON, VERIFY, or OFF. INHERIT inherits from the parent.
- `encryption` (Boolean) Enable ZFS encryption on this zvol at creation. Create-only: changing it recreates the zvol. Cannot be combined with inherit_encryption = true (the parent determines encryption).
- `encryption_algorithm` (String) Encryption algorithm, e.g. "AES-256-GCM". Create-only.
- `encryption_generate_key` (Boolean) Automatically generate the encryption key (key-based encryption). Create-only.
- `encryption_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) 64-character hex key for key-based encryption. Write-only: never stored in state. Create-only.
- `encryption_passphrase` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Passphrase for passphrase-based encryption (minimum 8 characters). Write-only: never stored in state. Create-only.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) When true, destroying (or replacing) this zvol also deletes all of its snapshots. Default false: the delete is non-recursive, and while any of those exist it fails and lists them. Changing it updates state only. It takes effect only once applied, so set it and apply before the destroy or replacement that needs it. Import sets it to false.
- `inherit_encryption` (Boolean) Whether this zvol inherits its encryption from the parent dataset rather than owning its own key. Create-only. Computed: reconciled from the zvol's encryption root on read, so it reflects reality even when left unset.
- `origin` (String) Snapshot to clone this zvol from, as "pool/dataset@snapshot" (for example truenas_snapshot.golden.id). When set, the zvol is created with pool.snapshot.clone and starts as a writable copy of the snapshot that shares its blocks until it diverges; the configured properties are then applied with an update. Create-only: a different origin is a different disk, so changing it replaces the zvol (the destroy half needs force_destroy = true). ZFS cannot destroy a snapshot while clones of it exist, so reference the truenas_snapshot here and Terraform destroys the clones first. Cannot be combined with the encryption inputs (a clone inherits the origin's encryption). Read back from the ZFS origin property, so an imported clone round-trips; null for a zvol that is not a clone.
- `readonly` (String) Mount read-only: ON or OFF. Null inherits.
- `refreservation` (Number) Referenced reservation in bytes (space guaranteed to the volume, excluding snapshots). 0 makes the zvol thin. When unset, ZFS sets it for a thick zvol and grows it with volsize.
- `reservation` (Number) Reserved space in bytes (guaranteed to this volume including snapshots). Null (unset) inherits.
- `snapdev` (String) Visibility of the volume's snapshot device nodes: VISIBLE or HIDDEN. Null inherits.
- `sparse` (Boolean) Sparse (thin) provisioning: the zvol gets no refreservation. Applied only at creation; changing it on an existing zvol is a plan error (set refreservation instead, or replace the zvol). When unset, and on import, it is read from the zvol's refreservation (0 = sparse).
- `sync` (String) Sync write behaviour: STANDARD, ALWAYS, or DISABLED. INHERIT inherits from the parent.
- `volblocksize` (Number) Block size in bytes (512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072). Set at create time only. A clone (origin set) keeps the origin's block size; configuring another value is an error.

### Read-Only

- `encrypted` (Boolean) Whether the zvol is encrypted.
- `guid` (String) ZFS guid of the zvol. Stable across renames; it is the resource identity (import { identity = { guid = ... } }) and also accepted as the import id.
- `id` (String) Zvol name (used as Terraform ID). Changes with name on a rename; the resource identity is guid.
- `key_format` (String) Encryption key format: PASSPHRASE or HEX (null when not encrypted).
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the encrypted zvol is currently locked.
- `pool` (String) Name of the pool containing this zvol.
